deep.reconstruction:
The page sets up a hierarchy of 'Teichmüller groupoids' in purely topological terms. It is the combinatorial and topological foundation for the program, developed on these pages, of describing the Teichmüller tower and its Galois action through cuttings of surfaces into pants ('découpages pantalonesques', next page).

(1) ST_top, the 'special oriented topological Teichmüller groupoid':
- Objects are pairs (X,S), where X is a compact oriented surface with boundary and S ⊂ ∂X is a finite set of marked boundary points.
- Morphisms (X,S)→(X',S') are isotopy classes of orientation-preserving homeomorphisms X→X' carrying S onto S'.
- The automorphism group of an object is the mapping class group of the surface relative to the marked boundary points.
- The full subgroupoid with S=∅ is written T_top. It is an 'open' subgroupoid, i.e. a union of connected components, since no morphism can change |S|.

Variant ST^±_top: same objects, but morphisms are isotopy classes of all homeomorphisms, orientation-preserving or not. There is a functor ε ('signature') to the one-object groupoid [±1] defined by the group {±1}. The fibre category over the unit is ST_top, so ST^±_top is an extension of [±1] by ST_top. This is the extended mapping class groupoid with its orientation character.

(2) The 'divided' variant, TD_top or STD_top (D for 'divisé'):
- Objects are triples (X,Σ,S): X is a compact oriented surface with boundary, Σ is a compact 1-dimensional submanifold of the interior X∖∂X (a system of disjoint closed curves, i.e. a cut system), and S ⊂ Σ ∪ ∂X is a finite set of marked points.
- Morphisms are isotopy classes of orientation-preserving homeomorphisms respecting Σ and S.
- Automorphism groups are stabilizers of a multicurve (with marked points on it) in the mapping class group. These are exactly the groups attached to boundary strata of the Deligne–Mumford compactification, i.e. to degenerate (stable) curves.
- ST_top embeds in STD_top as the open subgroupoid Σ=∅ (the margin reads 'imm. ouvert').

(3) The ± version TS^±_top ('biorienté divisé') is defined in the same way.

The previous page has analogous diagrams for groupoids of 'découpages' C_dep → C̃_dep with ± versions, fully faithful essentially surjective functors, and π_0 comparisons. The next page draws pants decompositions of a triangulated map. So the page serves to give the topological counterparts of the stack-theoretic Teichmüller groupoids of the Esquisse, including 'divided' surfaces needed to glue along cut curves.
errors: Notation is inconsistent: ST_top / T_top; TD_top vs STD_top in the NB; 3°) writes TS^±_top for what should presumably be (S)TD^±_top.
In 2°) 'compact 1-submanifold of X∖∂X' should mean closed curves (no boundary), otherwise arcs with interior endpoints would be allowed; this is not made explicit.

Whether the curves of Σ are oriented or unoriented, and whether morphisms may permute them, is left implicit. Since points of S on Σ must be respected, morphisms preserve Σ setwise with its marked points.
'Sous-groupoïde ouvert' is used in the sense of a union of connected components (full subgroupoid closed under isomorphism), not a topological notion. Correct but idiosyncratic.

ideas.what: Groupoid of compact oriented surfaces with marked boundary points, morphisms = isotopy classes of homeomorphisms (mapping class groupoid)
ideas.modern_name: mapping class groupoid / topological Teichmüller (modular) groupoid
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); later Moore–Seiberg, Bakalov–Kirillov, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), Teichmüller tower / modular multiplicities

ideas.what: ± variant with signature functor to [±1], fibre = orientation-preserving groupoid
ideas.modern_name: extended mapping class groupoid and orientation character

ideas.what: 'Divided' surfaces (X,Σ,S) with a cut system Σ and marked points on Σ ∪ ∂X, and their mapping class groupoid containing the undivided one as open subgroupoid
ideas.modern_name: mapping class groupoid of surfaces with cut systems / multicurve stabilizers (boundary strata of DM compactification)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions surfaces cut into pants and gluing, but not this formal groupoid as far as I know

missed.claim: An explicit formal groupoid of 'divided' oriented surfaces (multicurve plus marked points on the curves and on the boundary), with ± versions, is set up as the topological model for the Teichmüller tower. It anticipates the cut-system groupoids of Bakalov–Kirillov and the Lego formalism, but adds a marked point on each cut curve, which plays the role of a framing/parametrization data. This is a documentary priority detail rather than a new result.
missed.quote: (X,Σ,S) ... Σ sous-variété compacte de dim 1 de X∖∂X, S⊂Σ∪∂X partie finie ... 'groupoïde de Teichmüller orienté divisé topologique'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it shows that Grothendieck in 1983 formalized the stratified (divided) mapping class groupoids later used in the Lego–Teichmüller game and modular functor literature. Marked points on cut curves correspond to the choice of gluing parametrizations used in modular functors.

deep.surprise_reason: These are clean but essentially definitional set-ups of mapping class groupoids, with ± and cut-system variants. They are close to what the Esquisse announces and to what Moore–Seiberg and Bakalov–Kirillov later formalized. The marked points on cut curves are a small, unremarkable detail.

The arrow out of ST^±_top is labelled ε, with '(signature)' written beneath. The target is the groupoid defined by the group ±1, denoted [±1] ('unité' likely means unit object / punctual groupoid).
In 2°) the notation is written 𝒯𝒟_top with a crossed-out subscript; the NB writes 𝒮𝒯𝒟_top.
